from_node.description: An organization governs an AI system across development, deployment and operation using multiple trustworthiness criteria, oversight, accountability and lifecycle controls.

to_node.description: Because the system is computational, standardized and monitored, its organization is necessarily a pure instance of uncontestable total ordering that eliminates human agency and correction.

bridge.statement: Current AI governance frameworks explicitly model human oversight, accountability, safety, transparency and contextual criteria; these do not prove freedom from ordering pressures but they block automatic totalization.

to4.criteria_tradeoffs: trustworthiness criteria are plural and context-sensitive rather than reducible to one efficiency metric
to4.governance: formal governance processes allocate oversight and accountability
to4.control_responsibility: control is distributed and auditable rather than assumed to reside in the model alone
to4.corrigibility: monitoring, review, escalation and lifecycle governance provide explicit correction channels
to4.material_environmental_dependency: compute, data supply chain, infrastructure and institutional context matter
to4.native_method: AI governance standards / risk and responsibility analysis
to4.revision_trigger: evidence that governance mechanisms are purely nominal and systematically fail to constrain optimization/order pressures
